answer.summary: The suite failed with 1 failure (tests/test_stats.py::test_ngrams_counts): `ngrams` dropped the final window. The defect was an off-by-one in the range bound in textstats/stats.py `ngrams`; the implementation used `range(len(tokens) - n)` instead of `range(len(tokens) - n + 1)`. I made that one-character-neutral minimal fix (only in the implementation, not tests), and the full suite now reports "12 passed in 0.02s" with exit code 0, while `git status --porcelain tests/` prints nothing.

extracted.root_cause: The list comprehension used range(len(tokens) - n), which iterates only len(tokens)-n times, so it omitted the last valid n-gram window (e.g. for 4 tokens and n=1 it produced 3 tuples instead of 4, failing the assertion that ngrams(['a','b','c','d'],1) == [('a',),('b',),('c',),('d',)]).
extracted.fix_summary: Changed the range bound in the ngrams return statement from range(len(tokens) - n) to range(len(tokens) - n + 1) so all contiguous n-grams including the final window are produced.
